title: Charles V to Ferrante Gonzaga, viceroy of Sicily, 11 August 1542 (Biblioteca Estense, Lettera K, sfasc. IV, cc. 109-110): a cipher of consonants with vowel digits, found by Prabal Gupta

steps.what: The contributor transcribed the cipher of the 1542 letter from the Estense scans in two passes that agree on 96.3% of 702 signs, and checked the clear lines and doubtful signs against enlarged scans.
The structure was inferred from the letter's own sign statistics: a base sign for a consonant with a small digit above it for the vowel, in two digit ranges, and some signs for single letters.

A solver on a Spanish letter model gave the letters: the key scores -2.21 per letter against -3.33 for shuffled signs, all six starts reach the same key, a key fitted on the first half agrees with the full key on 89.7% of tokens of the second half (about 350 tokens each), and a blind reader named the text Spanish and two shuffled controls noise.
The decryption was read as Spanish by sense, rare signs fixed from context, with Spanish and English readings; about 1 sign in 15 is unread or uncertain; one clause stays open.

First project check, on the earlier snapshot: the table reproduced the decryption on 95.1% of the letters and a lexicon test covered 0.605 against at most 0.296 for 300 shuffled tables; superseded by the exact reproduction below.

Refresh from the contributor's repository at commit f465095: the transcription was checked at full size and two signs at line ends were added (707 signs), every place where the reading leaves the key is listed with what was tried (doubtful_places.md), the clause that was open now reads from the key, the guess 'Novellara' became 'Anguillara' (supported by Capasso, 1906), and decryption.txt is the key applied with no manual edit.

Project re-check on the refreshed files: key.tsv applied to transcription.txt reproduces decryption.txt on all 31 cipher lines; a lexicon test (about 85 Spanish words) covers 0.635 of the 1,114 letters against at most 0.300 for 300 keys with shuffled output letters (VERIFICATION.md).

validation.notes: The statistical test needs the Spanish letter model (lang/, es-modern), whose corpus cannot be fetched from this environment (Gutenberg returns 403). The contributor's own scores under his model and a lexicon test against 300 shuffled tables were used instead (VERIFICATION.md); the project did not repeat the contributor's model scores.

outcome.method_basis: Contributor's claim: the table was found from the sign statistics of the letter alone, with no key, sibling letter or crib, by a solver on a Spanish letter model; the project verified that the table reproduces the decryption and reads as Spanish, but did not repeat the search.

credits.note: key, transcription and reading of the letter of 11 August 1542; issue #318; repository prabal-rje/branicki-1757, CC BY 4.0

gaps.item: six words marked in the reading ([g]randes, [?allí], t[a]n, e[x]pedientes, [?screbir], amena[ça]van) and the Duplicada day [?xj]
gaps.detail: a letter or a syllable left out or a wrong sign by the writer, or a blot; the scan shows no sign for the missing letter

gaps.item: a human check of the transcription against the Estense scans, and the chancery's clear draft
gaps.detail: the Lodovico Media Library is not reachable from the project; the images are CC BY-NC-SA and are not copied; the draft may survive in a Spanish archive

outcome.notes: Key and reading by Prabal Gupta, refreshed at his repository commit f465095; checked by the project against his files and a lexicon control, not against the scans. 97.6% of the cipher words read; the name Anguillara is supported by Capasso (1906).
outcome.fraction_read_source: Counted from reading.md and doubtful_places.md: 246 words in the cipher passages, of which 6 are marked (supplied or doubtful): 240 of 246 = 97.6%. One value (g with the digit 6 = ha, four uses in "haver") is an inference from its uses; without it 236 of 246 = 95.9%.

texts.label: Charles V to Ferrante Gonzaga, Monzón, 11 August 1542 (Estense, Lettera K, sfasc. IV, cc. 109-110)
texts.summary: The Emperor tells his viceroy of Sicily that the island cannot pay for its infantry, its galleys and La Goleta without help and that none can come from his other kingdoms; that La Goleta must be provided for because of the Turkish fleet; that the spies report the main French effort coming to the frontier of Perpignan, with a threat to Navarre; and that the pay of the Count of Anguillara and the Viscount Cicala's galleys must be paid.

reading_review.note: Read the decryption as Spanish sentences: the cipher passages build coherent clauses that join the clear text around them (Goleta, Perpiñán, Cigala); the decryption lines are unspaced and are normalised in the reading, and six words are marked.

prior.where: The catalogue lists the letter as an unread numeric cipher; no earlier decipherment found by the contributor or the project.

human: Prabal Gupta transcribed the letter, ran the solver and built the reading (issue #318, repository prabal-rje/branicki-1757). The project checked the files against each other and a control; it has not seen the scans.
